title: Subtle header strips
direction: Layout: keep the original practical two-column layout. A wider left white bordered card holds the incident, operating contract and CTA; a narrower right white bordered card holds the working environment. Normal plain title and subtitle above both, duration aligned right. The only new visual design is a short pale-lavender title strip across the top of each card, using the chapter overview's 'Learn more' style. Each strip is 60px tall, with a small circular document or flag icon, and ONLY at the far right 2 or 3 very pale flat diagonal parallelograms. Content backgrounds stay pure white. No separate hero illustration. Very modest and believable, almost identical styling to an existing course overview.
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE full desktop screenshot-style design option for the opening page of the Materialize Learning Lab challenge. This is a restrained, realistic educational website UI, matching existing main and chapter overview pages. Landscape image approximately 1600 x 1050, enough height to include the complete page at readable font size. No device frame, browser chrome, labels outside the webpage, collage, or floating presentation stage. It must look like a normal live webpage designed by a front-end developer using simple CSS and small hand-authored SVG line accents. White background, thin #e3e1e9 borders, flat white cards with 4–6px corner radii, Arial/Segoe UI typography, near-black text, muted gray descriptions and violet #5528e9 accent. H1 about 38–40px, section headings 22px, body text 16px. NO oversized marketing headings. About 90–95% of the page visually white or near-white. Artwork is strictly a secondary accent taking under 7% of the page area. If a pattern is used keep it to a short band or tiny corner at about 4% opacity. No visual clutter. No glossy AI illustration, no isometric worlds, no shops or buildings, no 3D, no glassmorphism, no floating stacks, no strong gradients, no glows, no big purple panel, no decorative sparkles, no repeated ornaments throughout every section. 
Existing website style: slim white top navigation with a small understated violet geometric M icon, "Materialize", thin divider, "Learning Lab". On right "Docs ↗" and simple sun/moon icons. White page has 60px horizontal margins. Small muted breadcrumb "Learning path › Challenge". Chapter overviews use small pale-lavender horizontal "Learn more" bands with a simple document icon at the left and one very faint geometric shape tucked behind it; the main page uses plain white cards, fine borders, purple outline icons, restrained heading sizes and regular paragraph text. These existing elements should guide this design.
Render all briefing content clearly, preserving practical information. H1 "Save the Flash Sale". Subtitle "Investigate the discrepancy. Repair the system. Prove it is ready for the next sale wave." Small metadata "10–20 minutes · Chapters 1–8". Section heading "An incident from operations". Quote "Regional totals disagree with the latest paid orders during the flash sale. Can we trust this dashboard before the next sale wave?" Paragraph "You have inherited Northstar Shop’s dashboard. Investigate the system, make reversible changes, and hand over evidence that it meets the operating contract. Choose where to look and what to test." Section "Operating contract". Five normal bullet points, NOT numbered steps: "Paid-order counts and totals by customer region, during [event time, event time + five minutes)." "A correction replaces the previous version of the same order." "Normal snapshots are at most three seconds old. During the incident, a labeled ten-second fallback or unavailable response is authorized." "The application publishes complete results and never exposes a partial timestamp." "Operations and support share one durable result, with local serving indexes, within eight illustrative state units." Section heading "Your working environment" with these full three paragraphs: "Explore the data, deployed SQL, system observations, and application in any order. A notebook keeps the evidence you choose to pin." "SQL queries execute locally. Streaming, connection progress, and cluster behavior use the lab simulation. No database credentials or infrastructure setup are needed." "Pause at any time. Drafts and applied changes resume automatically. Hints and worked repairs are optional and recorded honestly." One normal-sized flat violet CTA button "Start investigation →", and "Back to main page" secondary text link. Do not add extra steps, fault hints, stats, hero marketing content, fake dashboards, or extra UI controls. The purpose is to improve an existing course briefing slightly, with subtle decoration and professional typography while keeping ALL details. Layout: keep the original practical two-column layout. A wider left white bordered card holds the incident, operating contract and CTA; a narrower right white bordered card holds the working environment. Normal plain title and subtitle above both, duration aligned right. The only new visual design is a short pale-lavender title strip across the top of each card, using the chapter overview's 'Learn more' style. Each strip is 60px tall, with a small circular document or flag icon, and ONLY at the far right 2 or 3 very pale flat diagonal parallelograms. Content backgrounds stay pure white. No separate hero illustration. Very modest and believable, almost identical styling to an existing course overview.

title: Small overview sketch
direction: Layout: borrow a chapter overview arrangement. Page title, subtitle and duration at top left; at the top right add ONE small flat violet outline sketch roughly 210px wide by 100px high showing just two small table rectangles joined by one thin curved line, a few row dashes, no readable data, no depth, no glow, no background pattern. This is the sole illustration. Under the heading row place two plain thin-bordered white cards, left wider for incident and operating contract, right smaller for the working environment. Use only small purple outline heading icons and thin dividers. Put the normal violet CTA under the operating contract. Retain lots of white space and modest everyday typography.
